text: Template-based transfer is the dominant route: TemplateTransfer transplants pockets from the single highest-identity template and reaches 0.55 top-1 pocket precision above 40% template identity, but drops to 0.41 below 30% identity because a single template often carries a partially mismatched pocket.
quote: On an invented benchmark of 80 targets it reaches 0.55 top-1 pocket precision when template identity exceeds 40%, but precision drops to 0.41 for targets below 30% identity

text: SeqPocket removes the template requirement, predicting binding residues with a residue-attention network; it matches template-based methods on template-free targets but lags them by 0.10 top-1 precision on template-rich ones and cannot localize pockets without sequence motifs.
quote: It matches template-based methods on targets with no usable template but lags them by 0.10 top-1 precision on template-rich targets. The authors note it cannot localize pockets that lack sequence motifs.

text: MultiTempl pools pockets from up to 8 templates and ranks them by frequency, raising recall by 0.15 over single-template transfer, but low-identity precision stays flat because low-quality templates vote with equal weight.
quote: Pooling raises recall by 0.15 over single-template transfer, but precision on low-identity targets stays flat because low-quality templates vote with equal weight.

text: GeoScore ranks pockets geometrically without any template, but reports no comparison against template-based predictors and no low-identity evaluation. ConsenSite scores pockets by unweighted consensus across homologous experimental structures, gaining 0.07 precision, but requires multiple structures of the target itself and was not evaluated on template transfer.
quote: the abstract reports no comparison against template-based predictors and no low-identity evaluation. | It improves precision by 0.07 over single-structure scoring, but requires multiple experimental structures of the target itself

text: A survey groups these methods into template-based, geometry-based and sequence-based families and identifies low-identity template transfer as the weakest setting.
quote: low-identity template transfer remains the weakest setting across all template-based methods surveyed
